pr.body:
## Summary This pull request introduces a new feature to manage calendar cache data, including the ability to view cache status and delete cached data. It also includes several supporting updates to repositories, APIs, and UI components. Below is a summary of the most important changes grouped by theme. ### New Feature: Calendar Cache Management * Added a `deleteCache` mutation to the TRPC `calendarsRouter`, enabling users to delete cached calendar data by credential ID. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsxR27-R33](diffhunk://#diff-9e053175cc6dfb5717313e0587a730fff132f9d3c1200204f0ce8dac53a19280R27-R33)`) * Introduced the `deleteCacheHandler` to handle cache deletion logic, including validation of user access to the specified credential. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.tsR1-R33](diffhunk://#diff-572888b8e0555167a5787847f29d5a46623eff170491acc0654e916f5b4afd18R1-R33)`) * Updated the `connectedCalendarsHandler` to enrich calendar data with cache status (`cacheUpdatedAt`) by querying the `CalendarCacheRepository`. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.tsR27-R39](diffhunk://#diff-3f6a556ad60f26d0162770fcd81b5bddeb6ab0437552ac792045c3cd2608d710R27-R39)`) ### UI Enhancements * Created a new `CredentialActionsDropdown` component to display cache status and provide options to delete cached data or disconnect integrations. (`[packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsxR1-R134](diffhunk://#diff-c78273434b95ab8276bb5eb24d9bc088b10af029388bdcd08cbe478f44269b31R1-R134)`) * Replaced the `DisconnectIntegration` component with `CredentialActionsDropdown` in the `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` UI, integrating the new cache management functionality. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L5-R5)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L70-L81)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L125-L135)`) ### Repository and Database Updates * Added a `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method to the `CalendarCacheRepository` and its mock implementation to fetch cache statuses for multiple credentials. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b36c72c0db751ba0cafe234dfa150817672869825333c22b074c4977a6135b8dR30-R32)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ceffbae9ef3da413495feac73a341672e77ffaf493cf67ada0b637ead80ded38R26-R30)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4cf8d3089fad7b6c8fe4172d8d42147f136b65baf30b726e57b9b10d179d4a99R172-R188)`) * Introduced a new `updateManyByCredentialId` method in the `SelectedCalendarRepository` to update multiple calendars by credential ID. (`[packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.tsR400-R406](diffhunk://#diff-ccb4eecfa701e5b0c7d6ba87dcc550cdf3700a63ee252849045611599ecb9273R400-R406)`) * Added an `updatedAt` column to the `CalendarCache` table in the database schema and Prisma model to track the last update timestamp. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9f597bd98bbcfdcf4861ee7bf0c238e7dfe54b456ceb69b852aaf3979c4102cfR1-R8)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-56fa4d384ba6fb94b130e9eb42c5cad00734b025ebd6c197f76873469725ae87R1718)`) ### Localization and Strings * Added new localization strings for cache management actions, such as "Cache Status," "Delete cached data," and "Cache deleted successfully." (`[apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.jsonR3376-R3382](diffhunk://#diff-57de4b8e5231f1d699891d98b0381d56e9e24537b0ca5420d1fba4f0597370bcR3376-R3382)`) ### Miscellaneous * Updated `package.json` to replace `ts-node` with `npx tsx` for running the `dev:cron` script. (`[apps/web/package.jsonL11-R11](diffhunk://#diff-14b60f636e1a2b0061da57aaf231cb1ed15a5dc0c592425ed82e58fec95d42d8L11-R11)`) ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human **🔴 High Priority (5 items)** - [x] **Verify deleteCache tRPC mutation exists** - The component references `trpc.viewer.calendars.deleteCache.useMutation()` but this mutation implementation is not visible in the PR changes. Check if this endpoint exists or needs to be created. - [x] **End-to-end testing with Google Calendar** - Install a Google Calendar integration and verify the credential-level dropdown appears, shows cache status, and deletion flow works correctly with confirmation dialog. - [x] **Test cache status display logic** - Verify that `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamps are correctly formatted and displayed only for Google Calendar credentials with actual cache data. - [x] **Confirm repository pattern correctness** - Test that `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` returns accurate data and the credential-to-cache mapping works properly in the UI. - [x] **Verify dropdown conditional rendering** - Ensure the dropdown only appears for Google Calendar credentials and handles edge cases (no cache, disabled integrations, etc.). **Recommended Test Plan:** 1. Connect a Google Calendar integration to trigger cache creation 2. Navigate to `/apps/installed/calendar` 3. Verify dropdown appears on Google Calendar credential with cache status and timestamp 4. Test "Delete cached data" action shows confirmation dialog 5. Confirm cache deletion works and UI updates appropriately 6. Test "Remove App" functionality still works correctly --- ### Diagram ```mermaid %%{ init : { "theme" : "default" }}%% graph TD UI["CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx
(New Component)"]:::major-edit Handler["connectedCalendars.handler.ts
(Updated tRPC Handler)"]:::major-edit RepoInterface["calendar-cache.repository.interface.ts
(Updated Interface)"]:::minor-edit RepoImpl["calendar-cache.repository.ts
(Updated Implementation)"]:::minor-edit RepoMock["calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts
(Updated Mock)"]:::minor-edit Translations["common.json
(Added Translation Keys)"]:::minor-edit UI -->|"Uses repository via tRPC"| Handler Handler -->|"Calls getCacheStatusByCredentialIds"| RepoImpl RepoImpl -->|"Implements"| RepoInterface RepoMock -->|"Implements"| RepoInterface UI -->|"Uses translation keys"| Translations subgraph Legend L1[Major Edit]:::major-edit L2[Minor Edit]:::minor-edit L3[Context/No Edit]:::context end classDef major-edit fill:#90EE90 classDef minor-edit fill:#87CEEB classDef context fill:#FFFFFF ``` ### Notes - **Session Details**: Requested by @zomars, implemented in Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/24545e0980df465995521419432a2a52 - **SelectedCalendar.updatedAt Usage**: Currently only updated in backend via Google webhook handler but not displayed in frontend. Frontend uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache. Consider if SelectedCalendar.updatedAt update should be removed. - **Import Path Resolution**: Had to fix UI component import paths during development - watch for potential module resolution issues in different environments. - **Testing Limitation**: Local testing was limited due to no installed calendar integrations - end-to-end verification with real Google Calendar data is essential.
pr.title: feat: add calendar cache status and actions

raw_findings.body: The handler still runs a CalendarCache groupBy query and returns `cacheUpdatedAt`, so the UI exposes cache status and a "Delete cached data" action for a feature that is turned off, and every page load pays for an extra DB query.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Feature-flag gating for calendar-cache is silently bypassed for the connectedCalendars endpoint.
raw_findings.impact: The handler still runs a CalendarCache groupBy query and returns `cacheUpdatedAt`, so the UI exposes cache status and a "Delete cached data" action for a feature that is turned off, and every page load pays for an extra DB query.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new enrichment code constructs the concrete repository directly instead of using the `CalendarCache` factory that gates on the global feature flag.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Obtain the repository through `CalendarCache.init(null)` (which returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the flag is off) instead of instantiating `CalendarCacheRepository` directly.
raw_findings.title: Cache status query bypasses the calendar-cache feature flag
raw_findings.trigger: A user opens the connected-calendars settings page on a deployment where the global `calendar-cache` feature flag is disabled.

raw_findings.body: tRPC maps the raw Error to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) instead of a 403/404, so the client cannot distinguish authorization failures and the error is logged as a server crash.
raw_findings.evidence: throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied");
raw_findings.failure_mode: Authorization failure surfaces as a 500 internal error to the caller.
raw_findings.impact: tRPC maps the raw Error to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) instead of a 403/404, so the client cannot distinguish authorization failures and the error is logged as a server crash.
raw_findings.root_cause: New handler does not follow the router convention of signalling client errors via TRPCError.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or `"FORBIDDEN"`) as the sibling handlers such as setDestinationCalendar.handler.ts do.
raw_findings.title: deleteCache handler throws plain Error instead of TRPCError
raw_findings.trigger: A user (or a crafted request) calls `viewer.calendars.deleteCache` with a credentialId that does not belong to them, e.g. an in-memory delegation credential id.

raw_findings.body: Those callers no longer satisfy `UserWithCalendars` and fail `type-check`/build, even though neither `updatedAt` nor `googleChannelId` is read anywhere inside this module.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cross-package compilation breaks for callers whose Prisma selects were not updated.
raw_findings.impact: Those callers no longer satisfy `UserWithCalendars` and fail `type-check`/build, even though neither `updatedAt` nor `googleChannelId` is read anywhere inside this module.
raw_findings.root_cause: The exported public type was widened with mandatory fields that the function never uses, tightening the contract for all existing callers.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Revert the Pick to `"externalId" | "integration" | "eventTypeId"` (or make the two new fields optional) since they are unused in this file; only widen it if the function actually consumes them.
raw_findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires unused updatedAt/googleChannelId fields
raw_findings.trigger: Type-checking any existing caller of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` that builds `allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` from a select that does not include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` (e.g. apps/api/v2 calendars.service.ts and event-types services).

raw_findings.body: An extra UPDATE touching every SelectedCalendar row of the credential runs on a hot path, while the value it is meant to refresh (`SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`) is never read by this feature — the UI cache status comes from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` via `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Write amplification on the availability path with no observable benefit.
raw_findings.impact: An extra UPDATE touching every SelectedCalendar row of the credential runs on a hot path, while the value it is meant to refresh (`SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`) is never read by this feature — the UI cache status comes from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` via `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`.
raw_findings.root_cause: A redundant bookkeeping write was introduced for a timestamp the feature does not consume.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove this write (cache freshness is already tracked by the new `CalendarCache.updatedAt` column), or if a timestamp on SelectedCalendar is genuinely needed, write it only for the calendars actually refreshed and only when the cache was updated.
raw_findings.title: Unconditional SelectedCalendar mass-update added to availability hot path
raw_findings.trigger: Every call of `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` (availability lookups, watch/unwatch flows, cron cache warming) for any Google credential.

raw_findings.body: The declared parameter type does not match Prisma's `updateMany` data type (`SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`), so either the assignment fails type-check or callers are allowed to pass relation writes that `updateMany` rejects at runtime.
raw_findings.evidence: static async updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId: number, data: Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput) {
raw_findings.failure_mode: Type contract mismatch permitting invalid Prisma payloads / compile error.
raw_findings.impact: The declared parameter type does not match Prisma's `updateMany` data type (`SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`), so either the assignment fails type-check or callers are allowed to pass relation writes that `updateMany` rejects at runtime.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new repository method reuses the single-record update input type for a bulk update operation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Type the parameter as `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput` (as `UpdateArguments` already does for updateMany data).
raw_findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId typed with SelectedCalendarUpdateInput
raw_findings.trigger: Any caller passing a nested relation update (e.g. `{ user: { connect: ... } }`), which `SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` permits, into `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany`.

raw_findings.body: The date/time is always rendered in US format inside an otherwise translated string, producing mixed-locale output (e.g. "7/15/25, 4:06 PM" in a German UI).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Localization regression in the newly added cache status UI.
raw_findings.impact: The date/time is always rendered in US format inside an otherwise translated string, producing mixed-locale output (e.g. "7/15/25, 4:06 PM" in a German UI).
raw_findings.root_cause: New component hardcodes the Intl locale instead of deriving it from the user's i18n locale.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use the active locale from `useLocale()` (e.g. `new Intl.DateTimeFormat(i18n.language, ...)`) or the existing localized date formatting helper instead of the hardcoded `"en-US"`.
raw_findings.title: Cache timestamp is formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
raw_findings.trigger: A user whose profile locale is non-English (e.g. de, fr, ja) opens the calendar credential dropdown that shows "Last updated".

raw_findings.body: The "Remove app" action is enabled for a delegation credential and firing it calls `viewer.credentials.delete` with a non-persisted (negative) credential id, which fails and shows "error_removing_app" instead of being disabled as before.
raw_findings.failure_mode: UI offers an action that always fails for delegation credentials.
raw_findings.impact: The "Remove app" action is enabled for a delegation credential and firing it calls `viewer.credentials.delete` with a non-persisted (negative) credential id, which fails and shows "error_removing_app" instead of being disabled as before.
raw_findings.root_cause: Replacing DisconnectIntegration dropped its internal `isDelegationCredential(credentialId)` guard and relies solely on the optional `delegationCredentialId` prop.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the previous safeguard by also checking `isDelegationCredential({ credentialId })` (from @calcom/lib/delegationCredential/clientAndServer) when computing `canDisconnect`.
raw_findings.title: Delegation-credential disconnect guard lost when delegationCredentialId is absent
raw_findings.trigger: A connected calendar entry produced by `getConnectedCalendars`' error paths (e.g. the "No primary calendar found" branch) which returns no `delegationCredentialId`, while the credential is an in-memory delegation credential with a negative id; the entry is rendered through the Alert branch.

raw_findings.body: The informational block behaves like a menu action: it receives focus in the arrow-key sequence and selecting it closes the dropdown without doing anything.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Keyboard/mouse interaction on a read-only element dismisses the menu.
raw_findings.impact: The informational block behaves like a menu action: it receives focus in the arrow-key sequence and selecting it closes the dropdown without doing anything.
raw_findings.root_cause: Static content was wrapped in a Radix menu item primitive instead of a label.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Render the informational block with `DropdownMenuLabel` (already exported from @calcom/ui/components/dropdown) or add `onSelect={(e) => e.preventDefault()}` and `disabled` to make it non-interactive.
raw_findings.title: Non-interactive cache status rendered as a selectable DropdownMenuItem
raw_findings.trigger: Keyboard-navigating the dropdown or clicking on the "Cache Status / Last updated" block.

raw_findings.body: The secondary timestamp uses raw `text-gray-500 dark:text-white`, which in dark mode is identical to the heading's `dark:text-white`, losing the intended visual hierarchy and deviating from the semantic color classes used across the codebase.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent theming and unreadable hierarchy in dark mode.
raw_findings.impact: The secondary timestamp uses raw `text-gray-500 dark:text-white`, which in dark mode is identical to the heading's `dark:text-white`, losing the intended visual hierarchy and deviating from the semantic color classes used across the codebase.
raw_findings.root_cause: New component styles bypass the repository's semantic color utility classes.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use the design-system tokens (`text-emphasis` for the heading, `text-subtle` for the timestamp) instead of raw gray/white Tailwind colors.
raw_findings.title: Hardcoded gray Tailwind colors instead of design tokens in new dropdown
raw_findings.trigger: Rendering the cache status block in dark mode.

raw_findings.body: `npx` performs an ad-hoc network download of an unpinned `tsx` version (or prompts/fails offline), making the script non-deterministic; the change is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature of this PR.
raw_findings.impact: `npx` performs an ad-hoc network download of an unpinned `tsx` version (or prompts/fails offline), making the script non-deterministic; the change is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature of this PR.
raw_findings.root_cause: Script now relies on `npx` resolution rather than a declared workspace dependency.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add `tsx` as a devDependency of @calcom/web and invoke it directly (`"dev:cron": "tsx cron-tester.ts"`), or drop this unrelated change from the PR.
raw_findings.title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` without declaring the dependency
raw_findings.trigger: Running `yarn dev:cron` in an environment where `tsx` is not installed in the workspace.

raw_findings.body: GNU sed treats the empty argument as the script/file operand and exits with an error, so `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never updated and the tunnel setup silently fails for non-macOS contributors.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Script errors out on GNU userland instead of updating the env file.
raw_findings.impact: GNU sed treats the empty argument as the script/file operand and exits with an error, so `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never updated and the tunnel setup silently fails for non-macOS contributors.
raw_findings.root_cause: BSD-specific `sed -i ''` syntax used in a cross-platform developer script.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a portable in-place edit, e.g. write to a temp file and `mv` it, or branch on `sed --version` / use `perl -pi -e`.
raw_findings.title: Non-portable `sed -i ''` breaks the new script on Linux
raw_findings.trigger: Running `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` on Linux (GNU sed) with an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=` entry in the env file.

raw_findings.body: The script terminates with exit code 0, so any wrapper (CI job, npm script chain) treats the failed setup as success and continues without a webhook URL.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Failure is reported as success to the caller.
raw_findings.impact: The script terminates with exit code 0, so any wrapper (CI job, npm script chain) treats the failed setup as success and continues without a webhook URL.
raw_findings.root_cause: A single unconditional `exit 0` is shared by both the signal-trap path and the error paths.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Accept an exit code in `cleanup` (e.g. `exit "${1:-0}"`) and call `cleanup 1` from the rate-limit and missing-URL branches.
raw_findings.title: cleanup() exits with status 0 on failure paths
raw_findings.trigger: The tunnel URL cannot be extracted or the Tunnelmole rate limit is hit, so the script calls `cleanup` from the error branches.

raw_findings.body: The warning claims the column is added without a default and will fail on non-empty tables, while the statement below actually adds `DEFAULT NOW()`; the stale text misleads about migration safety.
raw_findings.evidence: - Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Migration documentation contradicts the executed DDL.
raw_findings.impact: The warning claims the column is added without a default and will fail on non-empty tables, while the statement below actually adds `DEFAULT NOW()`; the stale text misleads about migration safety.
raw_findings.root_cause: The auto-generated Prisma warning header was kept after the SQL was hand-edited to include a default.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Delete or rewrite the generated warning block to state that the column is added with a `NOW()` default and is therefore safe for existing rows.
raw_findings.title: Migration comment contradicts the SQL it documents
raw_findings.trigger: A reviewer or operator reading the migration before applying it to a populated database.

raw_findings.evidence: return await prisma.selectedCalendar.findMany({ where, select, orderBy });

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Restore the `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` assertion on the argument object (keep the previous two-line form) instead of inlining the object untyped.
raw_findings.title: Removal of `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` drops type validation
raw_findings.trigger: Any future change to the loose `FindManyArgs` shape (where/select/orderBy) that no longer maps to a valid Prisma findMany argument.

raw_findings.trigger: Maintaining the calendars router, where every other procedure takes its schema from a colocated `*.schema.ts` file and the handler derives its input type via `z.infer`.

validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 1024 shows `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` with empty data object. This triggers an UPDATE on all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential just to bump updatedAt. The comment says it's for SelectedCalendar.updatedAt but the UI uses CalendarCache.updatedAt via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. This is write amplification with questionable benefit.

validated_findings.body: The declared parameter type does not match Prisma's `updateMany` data type (`SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`), so either the assignment fails type-check or callers are allowed to pass relation writes that `updateMany` rejects at runtime.
validated_findings.evidence: static async updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId: number, data: Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput) {
validated_findings.failure_mode: Type contract mismatch permitting invalid Prisma payloads / compile error.
validated_findings.impact: The declared parameter type does not match Prisma's `updateMany` data type (`SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`), so either the assignment fails type-check or callers are allowed to pass relation writes that `updateMany` rejects at runtime.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new repository method reuses the single-record update input type for a bulk update operation.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Type the parameter as `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput` (as `UpdateArguments` already does for updateMany data).
validated_findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId typed with SelectedCalendarUpdateInput
validated_findings.trigger: Any caller passing a nested relation update (e.g. `{ user: { connect: ... } }`), which `SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` permits, into `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 400 shows `data: Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` but the method calls `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany` which expects `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`. UpdateInput allows relation writes that updateMany rejects. The existing UpdateArguments type at L11 correctly uses `UpdateManyArgs["data"]`.

validated_findings.body: The date/time is always rendered in US format inside an otherwise translated string, producing mixed-locale output (e.g. "7/15/25, 4:06 PM" in a German UI).
validated_findings.failure_mode: Localization regression in the newly added cache status UI.
validated_findings.impact: The date/time is always rendered in US format inside an otherwise translated string, producing mixed-locale output (e.g. "7/15/25, 4:06 PM" in a German UI).
validated_findings.root_cause: New component hardcodes the Intl locale instead of deriving it from the user's i18n locale.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use the active locale from `useLocale()` (e.g. `new Intl.DateTimeFormat(i18n.language, ...)`) or the existing localized date formatting helper instead of the hardcoded `"en-US"`.
validated_findings.title: Cache timestamp is formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
validated_findings.trigger: A user whose profile locale is non-English (e.g. de, fr, ja) opens the calendar credential dropdown that shows "Last updated".
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 89 shows `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {...})` hardcoded. The component uses `useLocale()` (line 5 import) but doesn't use the locale for date formatting. Non-English users will see US-formatted dates in otherwise translated UI.

validated_findings.body: The "Remove app" action is enabled for a delegation credential and firing it calls `viewer.credentials.delete` with a non-persisted (negative) credential id, which fails and shows "error_removing_app" instead of being disabled as before.
validated_findings.failure_mode: UI offers an action that always fails for delegation credentials.
validated_findings.impact: The "Remove app" action is enabled for a delegation credential and firing it calls `viewer.credentials.delete` with a non-persisted (negative) credential id, which fails and shows "error_removing_app" instead of being disabled as before.
validated_findings.root_cause: Replacing DisconnectIntegration dropped its internal `isDelegationCredential(credentialId)` guard and relies solely on the optional `delegationCredentialId` prop.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the previous safeguard by also checking `isDelegationCredential({ credentialId })` (from @calcom/lib/delegationCredential/clientAndServer) when computing `canDisconnect`.
validated_findings.title: Delegation-credential disconnect guard lost when delegationCredentialId is absent
validated_findings.trigger: A connected calendar entry produced by `getConnectedCalendars`' error paths (e.g. the "No primary calendar found" branch) which returns no `delegationCredentialId`, while the credential is an in-memory delegation credential with a negative id; the entry is rendered through the Alert branch.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 68 shows `canDisconnect = !delegationCredentialId && !disableConnectionModification`. The claim is that delegationCredentialId prop might be absent for delegation credentials. However, looking at the code flow, connectedCalendars returns delegationCredentialId from getConnectedCalendars (CalendarManager.ts L65-66, L108). The error paths also return delegationCredentialId (L131). The guard appears sufficient.

validated_findings.body: The informational block behaves like a menu action: it receives focus in the arrow-key sequence and selecting it closes the dropdown without doing anything.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Keyboard/mouse interaction on a read-only element dismisses the menu.
validated_findings.impact: The informational block behaves like a menu action: it receives focus in the arrow-key sequence and selecting it closes the dropdown without doing anything.
validated_findings.root_cause: Static content was wrapped in a Radix menu item primitive instead of a label.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Render the informational block with `DropdownMenuLabel` (already exported from @calcom/ui/components/dropdown) or add `onSelect={(e) => e.preventDefault()}` and `disabled` to make it non-interactive.
validated_findings.title: Non-interactive cache status rendered as a selectable DropdownMenuItem
validated_findings.trigger: Keyboard-navigating the dropdown or clicking on the "Cache Status / Last updated" block.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 84 shows `<DropdownMenuItem className="focus:ring-muted">` wrapping static informational content. DropdownMenuItem (Dropdown.tsx L63-71) is a Radix DropdownMenuPrimitive.Item which is interactive - it receives focus and triggers onSelect. The content is read-only status info that shouldn't be selectable.

validated_findings.body: The secondary timestamp uses raw `text-gray-500 dark:text-white`, which in dark mode is identical to the heading's `dark:text-white`, losing the intended visual hierarchy and deviating from the semantic color classes used across the codebase.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent theming and unreadable hierarchy in dark mode.
validated_findings.impact: The secondary timestamp uses raw `text-gray-500 dark:text-white`, which in dark mode is identical to the heading's `dark:text-white`, losing the intended visual hierarchy and deviating from the semantic color classes used across the codebase.
validated_findings.root_cause: New component styles bypass the repository's semantic color utility classes.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use the design-system tokens (`text-emphasis` for the heading, `text-subtle` for the timestamp) instead of raw gray/white Tailwind colors.
validated_findings.title: Hardcoded gray Tailwind colors instead of design tokens in new dropdown
validated_findings.trigger: Rendering the cache status block in dark mode.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a stylistic concern about using raw Tailwind colors vs design tokens. While valid as a style suggestion, it's not a bug - the UI will render correctly. The category is already marked as 'style' and the severity is low. This is a code style preference, not a defect.

validated_findings.body: `npx` performs an ad-hoc network download of an unpinned `tsx` version (or prompts/fails offline), making the script non-deterministic; the change is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature of this PR.
validated_findings.impact: `npx` performs an ad-hoc network download of an unpinned `tsx` version (or prompts/fails offline), making the script non-deterministic; the change is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature of this PR.
validated_findings.root_cause: Script now relies on `npx` resolution rather than a declared workspace dependency.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add `tsx` as a devDependency of @calcom/web and invoke it directly (`"dev:cron": "tsx cron-tester.ts"`), or drop this unrelated change from the PR.
validated_findings.title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` without declaring the dependency
validated_findings.trigger: Running `yarn dev:cron` in an environment where `tsx` is not installed in the workspace.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The change from `ts-node` to `npx tsx` is a developer script change. While npx does network lookup, tsx is commonly available and this is a dev-only script. The impact is minor - developers can install tsx if needed. This is a style/preference issue for a non-production script.

validated_findings.body: GNU sed treats the empty argument as the script/file operand and exits with an error, so `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never updated and the tunnel setup silently fails for non-macOS contributors.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Script errors out on GNU userland instead of updating the env file.
validated_findings.impact: GNU sed treats the empty argument as the script/file operand and exits with an error, so `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never updated and the tunnel setup silently fails for non-macOS contributors.
validated_findings.root_cause: BSD-specific `sed -i ''` syntax used in a cross-platform developer script.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use a portable in-place edit, e.g. write to a temp file and `mv` it, or branch on `sed --version` / use `perl -pi -e`.
validated_findings.title: Non-portable `sed -i ''` breaks the new script on Linux
validated_findings.trigger: Running `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` on Linux (GNU sed) with an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=` entry in the env file.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 68 shows `sed -i '' -E "s|...|..."` which is BSD sed syntax. GNU sed (Linux) interprets `-i ''` as the script argument, not the backup suffix. This will fail on Linux with an error, breaking the script for non-macOS developers.

validated_findings.body: The script terminates with exit code 0, so any wrapper (CI job, npm script chain) treats the failed setup as success and continues without a webhook URL.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Failure is reported as success to the caller.
validated_findings.impact: The script terminates with exit code 0, so any wrapper (CI job, npm script chain) treats the failed setup as success and continues without a webhook URL.
validated_findings.root_cause: A single unconditional `exit 0` is shared by both the signal-trap path and the error paths.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Accept an exit code in `cleanup` (e.g. `exit "${1:-0}"`) and call `cleanup 1` from the rate-limit and missing-URL branches.
validated_findings.title: cleanup() exits with status 0 on failure paths
validated_findings.trigger: The tunnel URL cannot be extracted or the Tunnelmole rate limit is hit, so the script calls `cleanup` from the error branches.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 17 shows `exit 0` unconditionally in cleanup(). Lines 56-58 show error path calling cleanup when URL extraction fails. The script exits 0 even on failure, masking errors from callers.

validated_findings.body: The warning claims the column is added without a default and will fail on non-empty tables, while the statement below actually adds `DEFAULT NOW()`; the stale text misleads about migration safety.
validated_findings.evidence: - Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Migration documentation contradicts the executed DDL.
validated_findings.impact: The warning claims the column is added without a default and will fail on non-empty tables, while the statement below actually adds `DEFAULT NOW()`; the stale text misleads about migration safety.
validated_findings.root_cause: The auto-generated Prisma warning header was kept after the SQL was hand-edited to include a default.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Delete or rewrite the generated warning block to state that the column is added with a `NOW()` default and is therefore safe for existing rows.
validated_findings.title: Migration comment contradicts the SQL it documents
validated_findings.trigger: A reviewer or operator reading the migration before applying it to a populated database.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 4 states "Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value" but line 9 shows `DEFAULT NOW()`. The warning contradicts the actual SQL, which is misleading for reviewers/operators.

validated_findings.body: The compile-time assertion that `FindManyArgs` is a valid `SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` is gone, so such mismatches now surface only as runtime Prisma validation errors.
validated_findings.evidence: return await prisma.selectedCalendar.findMany({ where, select, orderBy });
validated_findings.failure_mode: Loss of static verification of repository query arguments.
validated_findings.impact: The compile-time assertion that `FindManyArgs` is a valid `SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` is gone, so such mismatches now surface only as runtime Prisma validation errors.
validated_findings.root_cause: The typed intermediate variable with the `satisfies` guard was inlined away.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Restore the `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` assertion on the argument object (keep the previous two-line form) instead of inlining the object untyped.
validated_findings.title: Removal of `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` drops type validation
validated_findings.trigger: Any future change to the loose `FindManyArgs` shape (where/select/orderBy) that no longer maps to a valid Prisma findMany argument.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The removal of `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` is a minor type safety reduction. However, the function signature still constrains the types via FindManyArgs, and Prisma will validate at runtime. This is a minor style/safety preference, not a bug that causes incorrect behavior.

validated_findings.body: The only guard preventing one user from deleting another user's calendar cache is untested, so an ownership regression (e.g. dropping the `userId` filter) would ship silently.
validated_findings.evidence: export const deleteCacheHandler = async ({ ctx, input }: DeleteCacheOptions) => {
validated_findings.failure_mode: Authorization regression in the new mutation would go undetected by CI.
validated_findings.impact: The only guard preventing one user from deleting another user's calendar cache is untested, so an ownership regression (e.g. dropping the `userId` filter) would ship silently.
validated_findings.root_cause: New security-relevant handler added without accompanying test coverage.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit test (prismock-based, as in packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.test.ts) asserting that a foreign credentialId is rejected and that only the owning credential's CalendarCache rows are deleted.
validated_findings.title: No test covers deleteCacheHandler authorization and deletion
validated_findings.trigger: A future refactor of the ownership check (`credential.findFirst` by `id` + `userId`) or of the deleteMany filter.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage gap suggestion, not a bug in the code. The authorization logic at lines 17-22 correctly checks userId ownership. Missing tests are a quality concern but not a defect in the implementation itself. Category 'test_gap' confirms this is about coverage, not a bug.
